title: Bound 4 Da Reload (Casualty)
label: East West
format: White-label vinyl first (about 1,000 copies, per Oxide in the Guardian interview); commercial CD single on East West (two parts) per Wikipedia

type.basis: A no. 1 garage hit built on a TV-theme and film sample. Sources file it as 2-step garage; one later reader comment calls it proto-grime. Held as an outgroup: a garage reference point against which grime's characters can be compared.

sound.text: Built around a sample of the BBC Casualty theme plus a spoken skit from the Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels soundtrack; Neutrino voiced it in one take over Oxide's beat (Guardian 'How we made' interview, c. 2019).
sound.pub: undated on inkl; Guardian 'How we made' piece c. Jan 2019 (mn2s post on it dated 29 Jan 2019)

sound.text: Tom Ewing (Popular, 2015) hears deep bass that leaves the track feeling empty and jagged, with time-stretched samples, skeletal keyboard refrains and gunshot sounds; the Lock, Stock sample 'blasts a hole' where the chorus should be.
Ewing describes Neutrino's rough, congested delivery as true to pirate-radio MCing: prepared bars, scatting, call-and-response and simply riding the beat (Popular, 2015).
Wikipedia's infobox labels it 2-step garage; many radio stations reportedly refused to play it because of the spoken sample.

context.text: Entered the Official Singles Chart at no. 1 on 6 May 2000 (15 weeks).
Began as a dubplate for a pirate radio show; the pair met at the pirate station Supreme FM and were members of So Solid Crew before signing as a duo (Guardian interview).
context.pub: undated on inkl; Guardian 'How we made' piece c. Jan 2019 (mn2s post on it dated 29 Jan 2019)

context.text: Dan Hancox (RBMA Daily, 2019) names it, with 'I Don't Smoke', as the straws that broke the camel's back in the 'garage wars' between the UKG old guard and MC-led crews; Timmi Magic dismissed it as 'kiddie stuff, going backwards'.
In the Guardian retrospective Neutrino says the track 'sounds like the start of what was becoming grime'.
context.pub: undated on inkl; Guardian 'How we made' piece c. Jan 2019 (mn2s post on it dated 29 Jan 2019)

uncertainty: Exact commercial release day not found (Wikipedia: May 2000; chart entry 6 May 2000). No catalogue number seen. The Guardian piece was read through an inkl copy with no date shown; an MN2S post about it is dated 29 Jan 2019, so c. 2019 is inferred. No contemporary (2000) source calling it grime was found; the grime link is retrospective and comes from the artist himself.
tracklist: Wikipedia CD Part 1: Radio Edit / 'Express Da Funk' / 'Bound 4 Da Reload'; Part 2: original, Remix, Video (enhanced CD). Also on the album Execute (charted 9 Jun 2001).
